Check joins and compare maps

Source: vignettes/audited-workflows.Rmd
audited-workflows.Rmd

Use this guide after Putting your data on a map. It shows how to check matches, compare years fairly and make small urban areas visible. All examples use data included in the package. For the enlarged map, install patchwork.

library(mongolmaps)
library(ggplot2)

Check what happened to every row

Prefer codes over names. If names repeat, use within to restrict the search to one area, or by_parent to supply each row’s parent.

district <- mn_join(
  data.frame(place = "Bayangol", cases = 12),
  "place", level = "soum", within = "Ulaanbaatar"
)
knitr::kable(mn_join_audit(district)[c("row", "x", "pcode", "status", "action")])
row x pcode status action
1 Bayangol MN1107 exact joined

The audit has one row for every original input row. It shows whether a row was joined, left out because it belongs to another level, or not matched. Save the audit separately if you need a permanent analysis record; rebuilding an object can remove its attached metadata.

mn_match(details = TRUE) shows the possible matches and spelling differences. A small spelling difference is not a probability that the match is correct.

Stop on uncertain or duplicate matches

strict = TRUE stops on unresolved names, fuzzy matches, missing boundaries and duplicate place/group combinations. In strata, list the columns that define separate observations.

observations <- data.frame(
  place = c("Uvs", "Uvs", "Khovd", "Khovd"),
  Year = c(2024, 2025, 2024, 2025),
  cases = c(10, 12, 20, 15)
)
joined <- mn_join(observations, "place", level = "aimag",
                  strata = "Year", strict = TRUE, fuzzy = FALSE)
knitr::kable(mn_join_audit(joined)[c("row", "status", "action")])
row status action
1 exact joined
2 exact joined
3 exact joined
4 exact joined

The counts here are made up to demonstrate the checks.

Use the same colours when comparing years

A value of 10 should have the same colour in both panels. Set limits and breaks explicitly, or use facets, which share a scale. Show just the two observed aimags so the comparison is easy to see.

observed <- joined[joined$pcode %in% c("MN84", "MN85"), ]
mn_map(observed, fill = cases, limits = c(0, 25), breaks = c(0, 10, 20),
       title = "Example case counts") +
  facet_wrap(~Year) +
  labs(fill = "Cases", subtitle = "Made-up data")

For categories, give explicit cut points in bins so intervals stay the same across maps. Use midpoint = 0 for a scale centred on zero, such as a change in rates. Keep zeros, missing values and suppressed values distinct. A map alone cannot show whether a rate is stable.

Handle Ulaanbaatar’s two NSO codes

NSO code 5 is the capital region and 511 is the capital at aimag level. Some tables put the same measure under either code. Check the table’s metadata before treating them as equivalent.

capital_table <- data.frame(
  Region = c("5", "511", "5", "511"),
  Month = c("July", "July", "August", "August"),
  value = c(10, NA, NA, 20)
)
capital <- mn_join(capital_table, "Region", level = "aimag",
                   strata = "Month", value_cols = "value")
knitr::kable(sf::st_drop_geometry(
  capital[capital$pcode == "MN11", c("Month", "value")]
))
Month value
July 10
August 20

The default uses a nonmissing capital value and fills gaps from the region. Conflicting values produce a warning. Use ub_policy = "error" to stop on conflicts, "prefer_region" to give the region priority, or "none" to handle the rows yourself. Do not add region totals to their component units; that would count people twice.

Enlarge Ulaanbaatar

Small places can disappear at a national scale. mn_inset_ub() adds an enlarged view without changing the coordinates used for analysis.

pop <- mn_example_population[mn_example_population$Year == 2025, ]
aimags <- mn_join(pop, "Region", level = "aimag")
mn_inset_ub(aimags, fill = value, trans = "log10",
            title = "Population, 2025") &
  labs(fill = "People")

The panels share a colour scale but have different geographic scales. You can supply finer urban data through ub; use the same measurement units in both panels. See Maps of Ulaanbaatar for detached district panels.

Compare district population trends

Each panel below shows one district. The charts use real NSO population observations for 2015, 2020 and 2025.

district_pop <- mn_join(
  mn_example_population, "Region", level = "soum",
  within = "Ulaanbaatar", strata = "Year", value_cols = "value"
)
trends <- sf::st_drop_geometry(district_pop)

ggplot(trends, aes(Year, value / 1000, group = pcode)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2015, 2025), expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "People (thousands)", title = "District population") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

All panels share a vertical scale, so their population sizes can be compared. For a custom geographic layout, mn_aimag_grid and mn_ub_grid provide approximate tile positions.

Show population with circles

Large rural aimags occupy more space on a map even when they have few residents. Size circles by population to show where people live.

pop <- mn_example_population[mn_example_population$Year == 2025, ]
aimags <- mn_join(pop, "Region", level = "aimag")
mn_map(aimags) +
  geom_sf(data = mn_label_points(aimags), aes(size = value),
          colour = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.65) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 16, labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "Population, 2025", size = "People")

Circle area represents population. Circles can overlap, so use the district trends or the enlarged map when you need precise local comparisons.

Check the boundary date and source

The year of a statistic is not the year of its boundaries.

knitr::kable(mn_vintages()[c("id", "geometry_vintage")])
id geometry_vintage
admin COD 2020; Ulaanbaatar khoroo-derived 2026
khoroos 2026 source snapshot; effective date unknown
codes NA
admin_high COD 2020; Ulaanbaatar khoroo-derived 2026 
knitr::kable(mn_provenance(mn_khoroos())[c("id", "effective_date")])
id effective_date
khoroos NA
codes NA

Only data-v1 boundaries are available. Asking for another boundary_version gives an error. Khoroo boundaries are unofficial, and their effective date is unknown. Compare historical data only after checking code changes and boundary compatibility.

Prepare to work offline

This optional recipe downloads selected files before you lose internet access, verifies them and turns on offline mode.

mn_download(c("admin_high", "worldpop_2025_1km"))
mn_cache_verify()
options(mongolmaps.offline = TRUE)

WorldPop years and resolutions are opt-in; mn_download("all") does not download them all. See terrain and population for the limits of population grids and area summaries.
